overview: White answers ...e5 with a King's Indian Attack-style set-up: g3, Bg2, Nf3, O-O and then e4 or c4. Black takes the centre with ...d5 and ...Nf6 and develops comfortably. The game is closed and manoeuvring, with White preparing the e4 break; Black has no problems and usually equalises.

white_ideas.idea: Nf3, g3, Bg2, O-O and Nbd2 followed by e4 in KIA style
Or c4 and Nc3 for a reversed Pirc/Modern setup

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...e5, ...d5 and ...Nf6 and develop freely
Challenge White's set-up with ...c5 or ...Nc6 and seize space

typical_structures.structure: King's Indian Attack structure with White pawns on d3/e4 and a g2 fianchetto; reversed Pirc or Philidor

character.notes: Quiet, manoeuvring play; hard to lose quickly for either side.

soundness.notes: Sound; objectively passive but not refuted.

structure.notes: Centre not fixed; flexible like the King's Indian Attack.

approach.notes: A set-up White can play against almost any defence, KIA-style.

level.notes: Clear plans, little to memorise; a good starter set-up.

structure.reason: A KIA-style centre that is not yet decided.

approach.reason: White plays the same set-up against almost any defence.

level.reason: Clear plans, little to memorise, like the King's Indian Attack.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes and aims for e4 and a kingside attack.
